claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMoNi alloy has a coarse-grained, homogeneous structure after vacuum arc remelting.
Adding 0.7 wt.% Zr to CoCrFeMoNi induces grain refinement.
Adding 0.7 wt.% Zr modifies the chemistry of the passive oxide film.
Zr-induced grain refinement increases the alloy hardness.
Higher hardness lowers the wear rate of the Zr-modified alloy.
The modified passive film forms more uniformly than the passive film on the Zr-free baseline.
A more uniform passive film improves corrosion resistance.
Excessive grain refinement can compromise the passive layer.
Zr-induced secondary-phase formation can disrupt passivation and impair corrosion protection.
Relative to Zr-free CoCrFeMoNi, the 0.7 wt.% Zr alloy will have a lower wear rate in room-temperature 3.5% NaCl.
Relative to the Zr-free baseline, the 0.7 wt.% Zr alloy will have a lower friction coefficient.
The Zr-modified alloy will show only modest changes in corrosion potential and corrosion current density.
Concurrent wear and corrosion improvements require controlled grain refinement without excessive secondary-phase formation.
The predicted behavior may fail at elevated temperatures.
The proposed controlled comparison uses identically processed Zr-free and 0.7 wt.% Zr CoCrFeMoNi samples.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially predicts concurrent improvement in corrosion resistance, but the predicted outcome specifies only a modest, directionally undefined change in corrosion potential and current density, while the uncertainty field allows corrosion protection to be compromised. Thus, the corrosion prediction is not consistently stated as an improvement.
